title: Check Palindrome
description: Given a string, determine whether it is a palindrome. A palindrome is a string that reads the same forward and backward.
input: A string that needs to be checked for palindrome.
output: Return whether the given string is a palindrome.

examples.explanation: The string reads the same from left to right and right to left.
The string reads differently forward and backward.
The string remains the same when reversed.
The reversed string is different from the original string.

constraints: The input must be a valid string.

approaches.name: Using Built-In Method
approaches.description: Create the reverse of the string using a built-in StringBuilder method and compare it with the original string.
approaches.whenToUse: Use when built-in Java methods are allowed and the goal is to write simple and readable code.

approaches.name: Without Using Built-In Reverse Method
approaches.description: Compare characters from the beginning and end of the string while moving toward the center. If any pair of characters differs, the string is not a palindrome.
approaches.whenToUse: Use when built-in reverse methods are not allowed or when demonstrating string indexing and two-pointer logic in an interview.

interviewTips: Be prepared to solve the problem both with and without built-in methods.
For the manual approach, compare characters from both ends toward the center.
Know why the manual approach can use O(1) extra space.
Be ready to explain the time and space complexity of both approaches.
